title: HP Sold $10.9 Billion of Ink and Toner
description:
HP sold 10.9 billion dollars of ink and toner. The printer was just the start.

Sources:
- HP Inc.: Fiscal 2025 full year and fourth quarter results (PDF): https://s203.q4cdn.com/918857832/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Q425_HP-Inc-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf
- HP newsroom: HP Inc. reports fiscal 2025 results: https://www.hp.com/us-en/newsroom/press-releases/2025/hp-inc-reports-fiscal-2025-full-year-and-fourth-quarter-results.html
- Wikipedia: Ink cartridge: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ink_cartridge

HP Inc. fiscal 2025 (year ended Oct 31 2025), from its earnings release: Supplies net revenue $10,916 million; Commercial Printing $4,633 million and Consumer Printing $1,153 million (printer hardware, about $5.8 billion together); Printing segment earnings from operations $3,118 million vs Personal Systems (PCs) $2,054 million on $38,532 million of revenue. Wikipedia (Ink cartridge): a study by the UK consumer group Which? found some manufacturers' ink can cost more than champagne; printer makers use a razor-and-blades model. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: HP sold 10.9 billion dollars of ink and toner. The printer was just the start.
The ink is the business. Not the printer.
The printers themselves? Only about 5.8 billion.
Actually, one study found some ink costs more than champagne.
Then the flip. Printing earned 3.1 billion. PCs, just 2.1 billion.

problems: The cover image fails to mention 'HP', making the topic unclear to a scrolling viewer.
The data in the charts is inconsistent and contradictory (e.g., one chart shows $1.8B for printing, another shows $3.1B).
The narration says 'Printing earned 3.1 billion' while the screen shows '$1.8B' for printing, creating a direct contradiction.
The visual style is inconsistent, switching between stock footage of people and abstract bar charts, which feels disjointed.
The 'SUBSCRIBED' button overlay in the final frames looks like a cheap, forced call-to-action that disrupts the flow.
eyes.best_fix: Standardize all financial data to match the narration and ensure the company name (HP) is prominently displayed on the cover image.
